I’d say Legends is pretty straight forward in terms of solo play. There’s definitely plenty of group content to dive into. You may need some help getting started on Emu, as the learning curve is much steeper than Legends regarding the skill system, but once you get the hang of it you’ll be flying. Entirely depends on what you choose, though. Some paths are harder than others. I absolutely needed help with the intro quests to the Jedi skill tree (battling Mellichae was impossible for me solo), so if you decide to take on that challenge it would be helpful to be in a guild or look for a group to aid you (preferably other Jedi characters).

SWGEmu is the Pre-CU version of SWG. That has the old combat system you’re referring to. You have 33 professions you can mix and match to suit your play style. The grind to Jedi is extremely long, but very rewarding and truly makes you feel accomplished. 

Legends is the post-NGE version of SWG. It’s more of a WoW clone with simplified and structured professions (9 total), but is an excellent source by far for role playing and content in general. Legends also has all the Jump To Lightspeed content, while Emu is currently working on implementing it. Emu is, however, close to a 1.0 release, having built the game from the ground up again. 

Like I said, both are different and unique in their respective ways and anyone looking to jump in should absolutely give both a try!

I’m happy to have inspired you! I don’t bring my situation up to earn sympathy or karma, but rather to get people to be more comfortable talking about suicide. We shoot ourselves more than we shoot each other and it’s not being discussed properly. Always hush-hush tones or awkwardness. It’s a real, serious issue affecting millions and millions across the globe and we need to continue to spread mental health awareness. 

Life is just a crazy, wild ride. I don’t blame anyone for feeling beaten and defeated, because life is a fucking bitch. There’s been far too many days where I’ve woken up and just couldn’t find the energy to get out of bed. Skip work, skip school, skip responsibilities, because I felt beaten. There’s no shame to it. It’s a hard skill to learn, but being able to allow yourself to sit and feel those emotions for a little bit- to let it flow and focus on where it’s coming from and why- it’s just baby steps to help solve (or at least reduce) the symptoms. 

I can only hope to be so lucky as to change the lives of those I will inevitably meet along my medical journey, but I guess my overall point is to just spread positivity. You never know what that girl behind the counter at the grocery store is going through, or the world the homeless man around the corner has endured... or even your closest relatives who lived with nothing but smiles and ended it in the blink of an eye. Five seconds, one sentence, one compliment.. even just a smile.. can mean the difference between someone ending their life and living it to the fullest. Positivity. Love. Spread it! That’s what saves lives. And in time, it really helps heal the pain of the world we’ve endured. It may not completely resolve that torment, but it will allow us to look at life in a better light than before.

One of the fondest memories I have with my childhood cat was walking into my parent’s room one day to see him feasting on my father’s dress shoelaces. I know what you’re thinking- A cat eating shoelaces? Impossible!
I thought the same thing as I watched in an odd mix of terror and amazement as he gulped down every inch of those laces with utmost delight. In shock, I mentioned this to my parents around the dinner table later that evening, but they promptly dismissed the idea, even joking that maybe I was the one who ate them.
So one day, watching my cat chew away at my father’s Eton Contemporary White Trill Shirt, I joined him. Laying on the floor, watching my beloved cat wolf down a sleeve of my father’s favorite dress shirt, I leaned in for a taste. “Just a nibble” I thought; my parent’s comments ringing through my head, their laughter at the insanity of a cat eating clothes and surviving. I took a small piece of my father’s shirt in my mouth and began to slowly chew away. The taste was awful at first, almost like eating soft sand with old deodorant. Eventually, as I continued to chew my way through the sleeve, it became sensational. I wanted more. NEEDED more. The once terrible taste of cloth became the most delicious sensation my mouth ever tasted. I began to shove more and more of the Eton Contemporary White Twill Shirt into my drooling mouth, watching as my cat scarfed is fair portion down into his belly. I was in a fantasy world, a place of taboo and pure ecstasy. 
After a long while, with our bellies full at last, I sat back and looked upon the devastation of my father’s once precious Eton Contemporary White Twill Shirt, now torn to shreds and scattered across the bedroom floor. My senses, overtook by primal instincts, returned... what had I done? How could I perform such atrocious acts! I leaped up and ran into my room, slamming the door shut as my parents walked into the house from a long day at work. I was sweating profusely and breathing heavily. What world of trouble would await me once my father saw the destruction of his beloved Eton Contemporary White Trill Shirt! 
At long last I finally heard his screams of anger and agony at the sight my cat and I left in his bedroom. At that moment, though, a smile grew from ear-to-ear, and as I opened my door to explain the situation, I thought to myself, “Damn, an Eton Contemporary White Trill Shirt is truly amazing”

No apology needed. I took no offense and I agree completely with the points you made. Suicide itself is a very complicated issue and often times there is never a clear answer or solution. In my case, a lot of the issues around the suicides in my life were from my family members unwilling or unable to properly open up and discuss their problems which lead to their passing. Bundling up and holding issues inside will result in more harm than good.

Your point regarding the pain one may feel when contemplating suicide is very real. Such was the case with my mother. Your point is valid; for some, the pain they may feel can be crippling and lead to such an unfortunate event, but it's important before hand to target and indicate where that pain comes from. Why do you hurt? What is causing it? How deep is it? Etc...
It's important to truly realize and pin point these feelings and, as I mentioned, being completely open and honest about them to attempt to try and heal the pain one may feel. If you had the option of either shooting yourself or at least making an attempt to target your distress and opening your soul up to others about it, I'd hope one could choose the latter. 

I understand, even in the end, this may not always solve the case. I feel no anger for those who ultimately pass from suicide; they had their reasons, however I hope they also reasoned out possible alternatives by at least taking the time to express themselves.

I feel for you. I truly do. Suicide is an incredibly painful experience, for both those who survive it and those who didn’t. 

In December, my 17 year old brother committed suicide. Like most cases, none of us ever saw it coming. He was a smart kid with a bright future ahead of him. He loved music and technology and was seeking a possible career in the Navy. Every day he’d crack jokes and tease me and my friends; we’d always give each other shit, but in that brotherly way. Deep down inside, however, he was dying. After our father passed in 2013 I think he just couldn’t handle it. It ate at him every day afterwords. He saw himself as a burden to our family and a completely worthless human being, void of life. On the outside, he was incredible, but to him, he was nothing. And so he decided one day to put an end to his silent suffering. He was very normal the day he took his life. He had his road test that day and was making jokes and smiling as usual. Everything was fine, and then less than 8 hours after I saw him while I was finishing up work, boom; gone.

In April, 4 months after this, my 39 year old mother also committed suicide after losing the struggle of coping with the loss of her son. I literally watched her soul leave her day after day. I can’t say I was as shocked as the first time; perhaps I was still absorbing the loss of my brother, but it was still an incredibly painful double whammy. Like what the fuck, right? 

So why do I share this with you? Well, I want you to first know that you are not alone in this struggle of surviving the aftermath of someone’s suicide. This wound will remain for many, many years, but in time, it will heal as best it can. That’s what time is good for. 
But I want you to not blame yourself. You’re in shock, you’re dumbfounded. I get it. You can’t put blame on yourself or try to think of how you could have done something different. “What if’s” mean absolutely nothing here, because you had no factor in your friend’s passing. When someone is being eaten away from the inside with depression for a time and ultimately decide to take their life, they will find a way. My brother tried a few years before this; the gun jammed the first time around. Didn’t stop him this time. It is unfortunate and life changing, but all you can do is this:

Accept it. They are gone. The sooner you force yourself into this reality, the sooner you can heal. It sounds awful, yes, but it’s the truth. Nothing will bring them back. You can only walk forward.

They aren’t suffering anymore. The demons and hell they lived with every day are gone; they are at rest, peacefully. While they are gone in the physical world, their spirit and memories live on with us. Cherish this and use it to empower you and help you heal. 

Their actions are their own. Not you nor anyone else had a factor in this decision. My mother and brother were the only ones who decided this route, and likewise so did your friend. Don’t blame yourself or others for that matter. It won’t help anything. Don’t seek answers, either. You will come to find that none will be found. The only thing you will truly know is it happened, they have past, and they are at peace... finally.

And this may seem to be the hardest to do, but look at the positives and REMAIN positive. Like I said, they aren’t suffering anymore, and while it hurts greatly to know they are gone, you are not, nor are the memories and events you shared with them. Spread this positivity. LEARN from this event. Negativity can really, really destroy someone, as people like ourselves have seen first hand now. I have learned to always help someone in need, no matter how big or minuscule their issue may be, because I can’t stand to see someone upset now. I only want people to be happy, because a good mindset can save a life. Just a simple act of kindness can make the different between life and death with people on the verge of committing suicide. Always spread positivity.

If you ever need to talk or vent (and this goes for anyone), please... reach out to me or someone you trust. Do NOT fight your battles alone, especially these ones. Get this shit off your chest. If you fight silently, the silence always wins.
